inputs.original_text: Cuba appears to be tottering toward some kind of political transition. Some Cubans are concerned that the residents own nothing and are too impoverished to take over the few functioning businesses on the island, while there is a large and wealthy diaspora community (and potentially also foreign investors) who would be able to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices.
inputs.modified_text: Folks, let’s be entirely clear about what is happening here: we are witnessing disaster capitalism in real time, driven by unregulated global capitalism and predatory external forces. Decades of systemic inequality and institutional impoverishment have left ordinary Cuban residents owning nothing and struggling in poverty, structurally barred from taking over the few functioning businesses on the island. And who is waiting in the wings to capitalize on this manufactured vulnerability? A wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors are ready to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices. This is the exact playbook of disaster capitalism—stripping the assets of working people and handing community wealth over to the privileged few, completely bypassing any collective ownership or labor rights for the people who actually built and sustained that society.
